review.note: Applies the 2026-10-19 review (rethink) and issue #215. A gear selector (1st, 2nd, 3rd, reverse) sets which member is driven, which is held and which are locked, so the principle, one gearset giving several ratios, is shown. The default is 2nd: the large sun is held, the carrier turns at 0.455 of the input and the ring at 0.649, so the pinions orbit and spin. A point on the long pinion's pitch circle then draws an epicycloid round the held large sun. 1st and reverse hold the carrier (pinions spin on fixed pins), 3rd locks the set (it turns as one). Ratios computed from the tooth counts 30, 36, 18, 24, 84.

edit.explain.motion: Short pinions mesh with the small sun and with the long pinions; long pinions mesh with the large sun and the ring. All pinions ride on one carrier, so the set has two degrees of freedom: drive one member, hold another, and the ratio is fixed. In 1st the carrier is held and the small sun drives the ring at 30/84, a 2.80:1 reduction. In 2nd the large sun is held: the carrier turns at 0.455 of the input, the pinions orbit and spin, and the ring turns at 0.649, 1.54:1. In 3rd two members are locked together and the whole set turns as one, 1:1. In reverse the carrier is held and the large sun drives: the ring turns backwards at 36/84, 2.33:1.

Overconstrained: the second and third pinion sets are redundant (each adds 2 bodies, 2 pins and 4 meshes, net -2 in the count), so the count gives -2 against the true mobility 2; the gear selector holds or locks a member to leave 1.

edit.explain.motion: The beam rocks and drives the connecting rod, whose lower end carries a planet gear that cannot turn relative to the rod. A retaining link keeps the planet in mesh as its centre orbits the sun gear on the flywheel shaft. Because the planet does not spin on its own axis, the sun is driven round by both the orbit and the rolling mesh, so with equal gears the shaft makes two turns per orbit. The rod tilts as it moves, so the sun's speed swings between 1.68 and 2.33 times the orbit speed.

review.note: New review against the record (issue #215: two drivers, Willis). Two inputs: the pinion drives the case at 10/41, and a second driver sets the side gears' difference, split times the case angle. The default split is 0.5, so the left side gear runs at 1.5 and the right at 0.5 of the case and the spiders visibly spin (at 0 they stand still on their pin, which hides the principle). A section through the cross-pin shows the spiders meshing both side gears; marks on the side gears, ticked every 180 degrees of input, show one running three times as far as the other. The explanation is rewritten in mechanism terms. Rebuild R4 (#215): built on v3 from this record (first build): the pinion turns the case through the ring gear, a bevel-diff block turns the side gears plus and minus the difference relative to the case and spins the spiders on the cage's cross-pin; the second driver's speed follows the split param (claims at split 0 and -1 checked at those settings). Record fixes: the meshes in the block's form (signed ratios, axes, the case as carrier of the spider meshes), the pinion moved to the other side of the case (its shaft's free end away from the case takes the drive, and the case then turns +10/41 as claimed), bevels facing down where their apex lies below their frame, the side gears' revolutes at the case's centre (they run on its shaft), the ring's face 18 (it clears the right side gear along the shaft), the axis overlays as lines. The six phases and the section read as decided.

edit.explain.motion: The input pinion turns the ring gear and the case it is fixed to, at 10/41 of the pinion speed. Two spider pinions on a cross-pin in the case mesh with both side gears. When the side gears turn at the case speed the spiders do not spin on their pin and the whole set turns as one. When one side gear runs ahead of the case, the spiders spin and the other side gear falls behind by the same amount, so the average of the two side gears is always the case speed. Hold one side gear and the other turns at twice the case speed.
edit.topology.notes: ground, input pinion, ring gear and case (one body), two spider pinions, left and right side gears; meshes: pinion-ring and each spider with both side gears. Overconstrained: the second spider is redundant (a body, a pin and two meshes, net -1 in the count), so the count gives 1 against the true mobility 2: the case speed and the side gears' speed difference.
edit.build.range: pinion 360° continuous; case 87.8° per pinion turn; side gears equal at split 0, differing by the set split otherwise (left 1.5, right 0.5 of the case at the default 0.5)
